title: Goal Five Phase 1 Capability, Asset, And Music Audit

gates.title: Authorized inputs and existing capability truth
Human treatment approval and Phase 2 handoff

workItems.title: Inventory every repository-authorized production input
acceptance: Every repository-authorized audio, model, animation, texture, image, video, shader, production pack, and derived input relevant to Goal Five has a stable identity, provenance, usage boundary, and availability result.
Missing authority, licensing ambiguity, broken references, duplicate assets, and materialization requirements are explicit rather than inferred away.
No external asset is downloaded, purchased, generated through an external service, or added to the approved input set.

evidenceRequirements.description: Content-addressed machine inventory of every audited authorized production input
Content-addressed human-readable provenance, authority, and availability review
Passing checkpoint record bound to the input-audit checkpoint

workItems.title: Audit the complete reusable capability and authoring surface
acceptance: Canonical registries, schemas, actions, CLI operations, runtime/render support, editor surfaces, examples, and existing production packs are inventoried from implementation truth.
The audit distinguishes ready capability, composition-only work, real reusable gaps, production-local direction, and forbidden duplicate ownership.
Likely gaps are prioritized by treatment value and criterion coverage without implementing speculative features.

evidenceRequirements.description: Content-addressed machine-readable capability and authoring-surface catalog
Content-addressed architectural review of ready capabilities, gaps, and canonical owners
Passing checkpoint record bound to the complete capability audit

workItems.title: Analyze and compare authorized 45–60 second music windows
acceptance: Every viable authorized track yields deterministic identity, decode, duration, analysis, and bounded 45–60 second candidate windows.
Candidate comparison covers energy arc, sections, phrases, beats, transients, spectral character, silence, and suitability for a coherent multi-act flagship.
The recommended window and alternatives retain exact source and frame/time coordinates; intended-audio preference remains a Gate 1 human judgment.

evidenceRequirements.description: Content-addressed deterministic analysis for every viable authorized candidate window
Content-addressed comparison and recommendation with exact source and window identities
Passing checkpoint record bound to deterministic music-window analysis

workItems.title: Author the frame-exact musical and act map
acceptance: The recommended window has frame-exact acts, transitions, phrases, beats, peaks, rests, and confidence/provenance for every landmark.
Macro, phrase, and detail response opportunities are expressed as production intent rather than hidden engine behavior.
The map is machine-readable, human-reviewable, deterministic, and suitable as the timing authority for treatment and later authoring.

evidenceRequirements.description: Content-addressed frame-exact machine-readable musical and act map
Content-addressed human-readable map, provenance, assumptions, and uncertainty review
Passing checkpoint record bound to the frame-exact musical map

workItems.title: Write the evidence-bound flagship production treatment
acceptance: The treatment selects one exact music window and defines emotional arc, act structure, visual hierarchy, palette, material, lighting, camera, transitions, density, and three-timescale reactivity.
Every proposed layer, component, graph, model, asset, media, compositor, and artifact role maps to an existing capability or the smallest justified reusable gap with a canonical owner.
Procedural, model-backed, shader/particle/instancing, complementary media, camera, graph, and compositor breadth are included or receive an explicit evidence-based exclusion for Gate 1.
Alternatives, risks, representative review targets, performance posture, and forbidden production-specific engine leakage are explicit; no deep aesthetic implementation begins.

evidenceRequirements.description: Content-addressed complete treatment and alternative analysis
Content-addressed machine summary of selected identities, roles, gaps, exclusions, and review targets
Passing checkpoint record bound to the treatment and its canonical ownership map

workItems.title: Assemble and enqueue the Gate 1 treatment review
acceptance: One compact review packet binds the authorized-input inventory, capability audit, exact music analysis, musical map, treatment, alternatives, assumptions, and unresolved human judgments by content identity.
The packet includes representative existing-capability frames or bounded visual references sufficient to judge direction without pretending a Phase 2 prototype exists.
A program-scoped human-validation question blocks G1-01, recommends one treatment, presents viable alternatives, and prohibits deep aesthetic expansion while waiting.

evidenceRequirements.description: Content-addressed Gate 1 review packet and representative visual references
Content-addressed exact Gate 1 decision request and safe-work boundary
Passing integration check record bound to the Gate 1 packet and human-validation request

workItems.title: Approve the treatment outcome and authorize its successor
acceptance: The product owner records one approved Gate 1 decision that names exactly one successor outcome: accept the exact treatment and authorize Phase 2, or authorize a bounded Phase 1 revision with the requested changes stated exactly.

The claimed G1-01 checkpoint creates and selects the immutable successor named by that approved decision: a Phase 2 program derived from accepted evidence, or a replacement Phase 1 program derived from the clean terminal P1-06 commit and bounded revision request.

The single Gate 1 validation remains pending through discussion or requested treatment changes and is resolved approved only when the product owner authorizes one executable successor outcome; resolving it rejected or changes_requested is a terminal safe stop that requires a separately designed and reviewed authority mechanism before any continuation.

All old-program completion and review operations remain explicitly scoped until its lease is released, and default preflight may select the successor only after this Gate 1 program is terminal, reviewed, clean, and unowned.
workItems.externalApproval: Explicit approved product-owner Gate 1 successor decision in the Codex task

evidenceRequirements.description: Explicit approved human Gate 1 decision naming either the accepted Phase 2 treatment or an exact bounded Phase 1 revision
Passing checkpoint record bound to the approved successor program and pointer handoff
